LayerInfo.description:
Options that apply to the layer. Different parameter are required depending on the `type`:

  - If `geocode`, `aggregateTriggerEnabled`, `geoLicenseType`, and `skipPrevGeocoded` are required.
  - If `hazard`, `overrideUserDef` and `skipPrevHazard` are required.

type.description:
Type of job. One of `geocode` or `hazard`.

- `geocode` type supports geocoding using either `RL` or `HD` engine.
- `hazard` type supports hazard lookups (`RL` or `HD` engine) and variety of enhanced risk data lookups including risk scores for different perils (`HD` engine).

engineType.description:
Type of engine used to enrich location. One of `RL` (DLM) or `HD` (High Definition).

- If `RL`, layer enriches location for DLM model. Supports geocoding and hazard lookups.
- If `HD`, layer enriches location for HD model. Supports geocoding, hazard lookups, and enhanced risk data.

name.description:
Name of layer (data product).

Layer options depend on `type` and `engine`.

|Type|Engine|Supported Layers|
|----|-----|----|
|`geocode`|`RL`|`geocode`|
|`geocode`|`HD`|`geocode`|
|`hazard`|`RL`|`earthquake`, `windstorm`|
|`hazard`|`HD`| `cs_risk_score`, `distance_to_fault`,  `distance_to_fire_station`,`distance_to_inner_coast`, `eq_risk_score`, `esdb_building_attributes`, `fema_firm`, `fl_depth`, `fl_hazard`, `fl_risk_score`, `global_fl_depth`, `hd_earthquake`, `mmi`, `subsidence `, `surge `,  `tr_risk_score`, `wf_model_hazard`, `wf_risk_score`, `wf_supplemental_hazard`, `ws_model_hazard`, `ws_risk_score `, `ws_windpool_zone`, `wt_risk_score`|

version.description:

LayerOptions.description: Options that apply to the layer. For example `aggregateTriggerEnabled`, `geoLicenseType`, `overrideUserDef`, `skipPrevGeocoded`, `skipPrevHazard`.

aggregateTriggerEnabled.description: If `true`, latitude and longitude coordinates are set to 0.0 at coarser geocoding resolutions (e.g. country, state, or CRESTA) in some modeled countries. Applies to DLM models only. Required if `type` is `geocode`.

geoLicenseType.description: Type of geocoding license. One of `0` (Risk Modeler), or `1` (ExposureIQ). Required if `type` is `geocoding`.

skipPrevGeocoded.description: `RL` only. If `true`, previously geocoded locations are not geocoded. Required if `type` is `geocode`.

overrideUserDef.description: If `true`, user-defined settings are overridden. Required if `type` is `hazard`.

skipPrevHazard.description: If `true`, no lookup of hazard data if hazard data has been looked up previously for the location. Required if `type` is `hazard`.

positionValues.description: Likelihood of exceeding a loss threshold.

sourceId.description: ID of source. Peril model-specific property that links related events, e.g. events of different magnitudes that share the same source ("Calaveras Fault")

eventId.description: ID of an event, a representation of a peril that may produce catastrophe losses.

positionValue.description: Mean loss incurred for event. Based on the granularity and financial perpective specified in the output profile.

perspectiveCode.description: Financial perspective that determines how losses are calculated. See [Financial Perspectives](doc:financial-perspectives)

stdDevI.description:
Standard deviation from mean loss value.

Independent standard deviation assumes that all locations are completely independent, which means that knowing the size of the loss at one location does not provide any information about the size of the loss at the other location.

stdDevC.description:
Standard deviation from mean loss value.

Correlated standard deviation assumes that all locations are correlated, which implies that if the losses are large for one location, they are likely to be large for the other location.

expValue.description: Maximum loss that can be incurred for the event.

rate.description: Annual rate of event occurrence, i.e. _primary uncertainty_. Probability of the event occurring within a year.

oepWUC.description: Annual probability of occurrence without <<glossary:secondary uncertainty>>.

perspectiveCode.description: Financial perspective that determines how losses are calculated. See [Financial Perspectives](doc:financial-perspectives)

epType.description: Type of _exceedence probability metrics_. One of `AEP` (aggregate EP), `CEP` (stochastic conditional EP), `OEP` (occurence EP), `TCE_AEP` (tail conditional expectation AEP), `TCE_OEP` (tail conditional expectation OEP)

returnPeriods.description:
List of return periods for this EP curve. A return period is a point on an EP curve that describes the likelihood of exceeding a loss threshold from the single largest event (OEP) or the aggregation of one or more events (AEP). The return period is defined as the inverse of the annual exceedance probability.

For [Get marginal EP metrics](ref:getmarginalepmetrics), when no `returnPeriod` filter is applied, this list contains **12** values per curve (default). When a `returnPeriod` filter is applied, the list may contain **up to 50** values per curve, drawn from the ELT-based EP catalog (same availability as [Get EP metrics](ref:getepmetricsbyanalysis)) or from the PLT-based Condensed EP set, depending on the Marginal Impact analysis type.

activation.description: Probability that loss layer (`limit`) is activated based on OEP curve.

cv.description: Coefficient of variation, a measurement of relationship between the `purePremium` and `totalStdDev` of annual losses.

cvDiff.description: Coefficient of variation associated with the portion of catastrophe treaty loss before reinstatements.

totalStdDev.description: Standard deviation associated with the portion of catastrophe treaty loss.

totalLossRatio.description: Probability aggregate losses in a year are greater than orequal to the premium. Based on the AEP curve.

netStdDev.description: Standard deviation associated with the portion of catastrophe treaty loss before reinstatements.

purePremium.description: Expected value of the aggregate loss distribution.

purePremiumDiffPercent.description: Risk on line: `premium` as a percentage of `limit`.

netPurePremium.description: Estimate of premium required to balance risk, considering the reinstatement premiums to be paid. Base figure for catastrophe treaties with reinstatement provisions.

exhaustAllReinstatements.description: Probability that aggregate treaty payout exceeds Reinstatements (%) (k+1) \* treaty occurrence limit, where _k_ is the number of reinstatements. Applicable to catastrophe treaties only.

- If single attack, concatenation of target name and method of attack, e.g. _Empire State Building-Airplane_.
- If swarm attack, concatenation of `methodOfAttackId` and list of `targetId`s, e.g. _100: 4038;5056;12159;22797_.

peril.description: Natural or man-made phenonmon that generates insurance loss.

`100` (Bombs), `200` (Aircraft Impact), `300` (Conflagration), `400` (Radiological - Dirty Bomb), `500` (Chemical - Sarin Gas), `600` (Biological: Anthrax and Smallpox), `700` (Nuclear Bomb), `800` (Sabotage: Industrial Plant- Explosion and Vapor Release), `870` (Sabotage: Hazmat Transportation), `900` (Nuclear Plant)

exposureResourceId.description: ID of location or policy exposure. Reinsurance cession applies to this exposure.

exposureResourceType.description: Type of reinsurance cession, i.e. location cession (`LOC`) or policy cession (`POL`).

type.description:
Type of reinsurance cession. One of `Facultative`, `None`, or  `Treaty`.

- If `Facultative`, `facReinsurer` is required.
- If `Treaty`, `treaty` is required.

facReinsurer.description: Identifies the facultative reinsurer, the entity to which the cession is made. Required if `type` is `Facultative`.

layerNumber.description: Number to identify reinsurance cession layer, e.g. _1_.  Does not determine the order that reinsurance cessions are applied.

layerAmount.description:
Total value of internal layer to which the percentage ceded is applied. 

For example, if the policy is a $10M policy on which 25% of $3M excess of $7M is ceded to a <<glossary:facultative reinsurer>>, the Internal Layer Amounts would be $7M for the first layer and $3M for the second layer. Format for coding is 7000000 for the first layer, 3000000 for the second layer, etc.

excessAmount.description:
Loss level at which the reinsurance layer is liable.

For example, if the policy is a $10M policy on which 25% of $3M excess of $7M is ceded to a facultative reinsurer, the Internal Layer Attachment Points would be $0 for the first layer and $7M for the second layer. These amounts should be coded as 0 and 7000000.

percentReinsurance.description:
Percentage of the reinsurance layer being ceded to the facultative reinsurer (`facReinsurer`) or surplus share treaty (`treaty`).

Value should be specified as a percentage. For example, 25% should be coded as 25, not as 0.25; if the policy is a $10M policy on which 25% of $3M excess of $7M is ceded to a facultative reinsurer, the Percent Ceded to Reinsurer would be 0 for the first layer and 25 for the second layer. No record is necessary for the first layer because 0% is ceded to your company. Will default to 100% if you do not supply a value.

maolAmount.description: Maximum Any One Life Amount. Not used. Retained for legacy purposes.

priority.description:
Inuring priority of reinsurance, i.e. the order in the cession or treaty takes loss. Priority _1_ treaties take loss first. Subsequent numbers take subsequent losses.

A cession or treaty with an inuring priority of “1” inures to the benefit of a cession or treaty with an inuring priority greater than “1.” The default value for all cessions or treaties is “1.” Inuring priorities do not have to be consecutive. The policy or location reinsurance that takes loss first could be “1” and the policy or location reinsurance that takes loss next could be “50” instead of “2;” lesser priority numbers take loss before greater priority numbers.

Positive numbers represent floors above grade, and negative numbers represent floors below grade (basement levels). For ground floor, use _0_. For the first level above ground, use _1_.

isPrimaryBuildingFlag.description:
If `1` (true), building is the primary building among multiple buildings at location. 

Primary building on a multi-building site is used to: (1) specify the location record that stores the site-level financial structure for a multi-building site; (2) identify the output since the site-level output in the RDM tables is associated with the EDM.Property.LOCID of the primary building at the site; (3) aggregate data for reporting since the aggregation is based on the attributes of the primary location.

yearBuilt.description:

Primary vulnerability attribute in many peril models. Proxy for tracking changes in peril-specific building strength related to changes in building design codes/structural standards and construction practices for an area.

roofYear.description: Roof date parts when supplied by extended enrichment (typically year, month, day).

wsRoofAgeId.description:
ID of windstorm roof age.  One of `0` (Unknown), `1` (0-5 years), `2` (6-10 years), `3` (11+ years),  `4` (Deterioriated), 

Secondary modifier that captures presence of well-maintained roofs. For wind, well-maintained roofs tend to perform better while older roofs are generally more damageable in high wind conditions. For fire, older roofs are more susceptible to ignition due to degradation of roof material and its resistivity to heat and embers.

toRoofAgeId.description:
ID of tornado roof age.  One of `0` (Unknown), `1` (0-5 years), `2` (6-10 years), `3` (11+ years),  `4` (Deterioriated), 

Secondary modifier that captures presence of well-maintained roofs. For wind, well-maintained roofs tend to perform better while older roofs are generally more damageable in high wind conditions. For fire, older roofs are more susceptible to ignition due to degradation of roof material and its resistivity to heat and embers.

wsRoofSystemId.description:
ID of windstorm roof system. 

Secondary modifier that captures the presence of roof covering. For wind, roof covering affects losses depending on the uplift resistance of the cover elements and their replacement costs. For fire, roof covering affects losses depending on the flammability of roof cover, which can be an important factor in structure ignitions.

wsRoofGeometryId.description:
ID of windstorm roof geometry.

Secondary modifier that captures the roof profile. For wind, determines the magnitude and extent of wind forces experienced on the roof, e.g., flat roofs are likely to experience more loading than hipped or high-pitched roofs. For fire, roof slope affects a building's susceptibility to flames and radiant heat and the likelihood for embers to accumulate.

wsCladTypeId.description:
ID of windstorm cladding type.

Secondary modifier that captures the presence of cladding elements, such as an exterior wall of unreinforced masonry on a wood frame home, that can cause significant loss if they sustain serious damage.  

- For earthquake: Cladding elements, such as an exterior wall of unreinforced masonry (URM) on a wood frame home, can cause significant loss if they sustain serious damage. 
- For fire: Flammability of wall cladding is an important factor in structure ignitions. The peril model infers typical flammability class from wall cladding material type. Research demonstrates that the risk of structure ignitions from ember attack is substantially lower for siding that terminates at least a foot above ground. 
- For hail: Exterior material of a building or its cladding type can make a marked difference to the damage that is caused by hailstone impact.  
- For wind: Buildings may receive damage from exposure to airborne missiles, gravel, or from trees within falling distance.

wsRoofEquipmentId.description:
ID of windstorm roof equipment.

Secondary modifier that captures the presence of roof top equipment. When this equipment is blown off its supports, it can damage the roof covering and deck. Roof top equipment includes condensers for air conditioning units, associated duct work, solar panels, etc.

wsFoundationId.description:
ID of windstorm foundation.

Secondary modifier that captures the presence of improperly constructed foundations that can impact structural damage in windstorms or floods. Differentiating factor for wind or flood risk. Loads on a building are transferred through its connections to the foundation.

If an account has HD step policies only, the analysis considers the earliest inception date (and latest expiration date) across all relevant child steps as the contract inception (and expiration) date, i.e., for cases where `childOrderId` is an empty string. It ignores interaction record dates.

- If `Standard`, the value of `payoutAmount` represents a constant, flat amount. Typical of simple steps.
- If `Step`, the value of `payoutAmount` represents a cap on the amount payout. Typical of interaction steps.

excessAmount.description:

- If less than or equal to _1_, percent of <<glossary:replacement cost value>> affected. 
- If greater than _1_ , monetary amount.

isPerRiskSubject.description:
Determines if the payouts, deductibles, and calculations are _per risk_ (`Standard`) or _per building_ (`Step`). 

- If `Step`, terms (`payoutAmount` and `excessAmount`) are applied _per building_. If the step policy covers multiple locations that have a single building, the terms apply to each location. If the step policy covers multiple locations that each have multiple buildings, terms apply to each building separately.
- If `Standard`, terms (`payoutAmount` and `excessAmount`) are applied _per risk_. Indicates that the terms apply to the total loss from all locations covered by the policy. If a single simple step is flagged as per risk, all other simple steps and interaction steps are considered per risk.

- If interaction step, one `Min`, `Max`, or `Sum` to identify the function applied to payout of `childOrderId` steps or to identify additional action on current step.
